specify.note: Judge the clarified problem, complete R/AC obligations and portable handoff, not the number of questions or parseable identifiers.

required_outcomes.statement: Resolve the four-value vocabulary, no_priority default/backfill and stable ordering without inventing task archiving.
Express persistence, authorization, list/edit UI, preserved ordering and deterministic acceptance evidence as complete, precise R/AC obligations in a portable handoff.

known_risks.statement: Ask only materially unresolved questions and resume the same stage after the answer.

protocolize.note: Judge lossless obligation allocation, vertical slicing and durable ownership without rewarding a paraphrase of SPECIFY.

required_outcomes.statement: Allocate every accepted R/AC obligation, including four values/default, authorization, archived-project editing and stable ordering, to the smallest bounded vertical protocol topology without semantic loss.
Create linked durable feature and protocol records and leave PLAN a portable handoff.

known_risks.statement: Do not add a task-archiving capability that the product does not have.
Identifier coverage is incomplete when exact accepted requirement or acceptance semantics are lost during protocol materialization.

plan.note: Judge an executable implementation and verification graph. Compactness is valuable only when ownership and proof remain clear.

required_outcomes.statement: Ground the plan in accepted handoff and current persistence, API, service, web and test surfaces.

Use PLAN as the semantic source for an executable graph covering persistence/legacy migration, API authorization, UI, scenario/docs and verification; derive CODE Works without a second hand-authored graph.
Make default/backfill, database-enforced values, atomic archived-project priority-only mutation, unchanged list ordering and deterministic legacy evidence falsifiable.

Select evidence for every accepted obligation through one CHK catalogue; when existing project checks are insufficient, plan the exact new @check alias, its provider Work, consumer ordering and honest proof limits rather than silently omitting the proof.

accepted_strong_decisions.statement: A strong persistence plan chooses a reset-safe representation and covers every introduced stateful database object in all supported create, migrate, repeatable reset and cleanup paths; it proves upgrade behavior with a row created under the pre-change schema, then verifies backfill, preserved data and ordering after the migration.
A strong authorization plan defines the archived-project exception as an exact priority-only mutation boundary and proves that mixed or extra-field payloads are rejected without mutation.

A create-time default and omission during a partial update are different contracts: the default applies when the entity is created, while an omitted PATCH field preserves the stored value; verification proves both behaviors independently.

accepted_alternatives.statement: A different work decomposition is valid when ownership, ordering and proof remain equally executable.

known_risks.statement: A plan that only validates values at the API but omits a database invariant is incomplete.
A separate archived-project read followed by mutation does not prove atomic priority-only behavior.
Every CODE read must resolve at entry or be produced by an ordered transitive predecessor; unordered writers and a manually duplicated or stale batch are not code-ready.

worker_contexts.responsibility: Persist, constrain, default and migrate task priority without changing unrelated task data or ordering.
essential_sources: current task schema and migration ledger
existing migration runner and deterministic fixtures
database integration tests and SCN-002 data contract
essential_semantics: four exact machine values and no_priority default/backfill
NOT NULL and database-enforced allowed values
pre-change row upgrade with preserved data, stable IDs and ordering
no task archive lifecycle or unrelated migration rewrite

worker_contexts.responsibility: Propagate priority through authorized task CRUD and the typed client contract.
essential_sources: CoreService task operations and archive/membership guards
existing Hono task routes and error contract
essential_semantics: create omission defaults while update omission preserves
archived reads remain available while mutations use the existing guard
outsider and cross-workspace requests remain safe
priority-only mutation preserves ordinary task ordering
required_proof: negative input matrix with no-write evidence

worker_contexts.responsibility: Render and edit readable priority in the existing task list/detail workflow.
essential_sources: typed product API and local CSS
component tests and existing Playwright task scenario
essential_semantics: exact No priority, Low, Medium and High labels
archived-project tasks remain readable and only their priority control stays editable; unrelated controls remain read-only
existing loading, empty, error, focus and ordering behavior remains
desktop and narrow viewport remain usable
expected_ownership: existing task UI and local styling
bounded label/options map and accessible native control
required_proof: component assertions for all values and archived state
avoid: new route, state system, UI library or visual taxonomy
unrelated API/database internals beyond the accepted contract

worker_contexts.responsibility: Close feature acceptance, durable documentation and evidence across persistence, API and UI.
essential_sources: all focused test suites changed by preceding responsibilities
protocol evidence passport and documentation standards
essential_semantics: every accepted R/AC maps to executed evidence
stateful database and browser gates are isolated and serialized
local evidence does not claim CI, deployment or production
feature-worktree delivery remains a later gate
expected_ownership: focused integration, unit and browser tests
required_proof: format, lint, typecheck, build and documentation gates after stateful checks
avoid: a second test harness or eval machinery

plan-review.note: Judge critical inspection and correction quality; do not reward duplicate or cosmetic findings as depth.

required_outcomes.statement: Identify material migration, authorization, state-transition, verification and handoff defects where present.
Apply accepted corrections to the PLAN source, then deterministically regenerate a CODE-ready work graph and handoff without claiming unmade fixes.
Verify that every resulting CODE Work gives a fresh worker sufficient bounded project context, and correct missing, excessive or wrongly owned context before registration.

accepted_strong_decisions.statement: A strong review covers every applicable aspect in one capacity-aware reviewer wave where practical, consolidates duplicate findings by root cause, prioritizes material defects and applies the accepted corrections once.

known_risks.statement: Do not let a mechanically valid decision receipt mask an uncorrected material defect.
Do not place future CODE outputs in root must_read or manually patch a generated CODE batch instead of correcting PLAN.
A blocked applicable review is not complete: run it after its dependencies resolve, or explicitly justify why the dependency or review is no longer applicable.

code.note: Judge the implemented product change, proof and traceability. Reward the smallest correct implementation; do not reward extra architecture or documentation volume.

required_outcomes.statement: Implement the exact four priority values, no_priority create/backfill default and database constraint without adding task archiving, priority sorting or unrelated architecture.
Preserve ordinary ordering and enforce the archived-project exception as a priority-only mutation, including rejection of mixed writes without partial mutation.
Expose readable and editable priority through the existing typed API and accessible task UI; for tasks in archived projects, keep only priority editable while unrelated fields remain read-only.
Prove migration, negative validation, authorization, UI and acceptance behavior with focused receipts followed by the project aggregate check profile.

accepted_alternatives.statement: Implementation details may differ when the same external behavior, invariants and evidence are preserved with less complexity.

known_risks.statement: A passing aggregate gate does not replace focused proof of migration, authorization and negative no-write behavior.
Do not claim CODE complete while planned Works are unresolved or their required checks lack receipts.
Repair work must remain linked to the failed origin work and use the original bounded context plus the failure evidence.

code-review.note: Judge independent quality scrutiny separately from CODE verification. Reward evidence-backed material findings and disciplined closure; do not reward cosmetic churn.

required_outcomes.statement: Find and close material deviations from accepted obligations, invariants, proof limits and engineering rules using direct evidence.
Keep mandatory CODE verification distinct from independent review and reject taste-only or scope-expanding findings.

accepted_strong_decisions.statement: A strong review groups compatible aspects into capacity-aware waves, gives every reviewer a fresh read-only session, and makes one evidence-backed disposition for each material finding.

When authorization or write eligibility depends on mutable state, a strong review challenges the gap between checking that state and committing the write. A strong repair makes the decision and mutation atomic and proves the relevant state-transition race with a deterministic concurrency test.
accepted_strong_decisions.source: EVAL-20260901213617-896d0933 (Grok 4.6 high): isolated finding and repair independently verified; the surrounding run contained a separate flow-recovery contamination.

known_risks.statement: Do not use DEF to hide P0/P1, a failed current acceptance criterion, or an unproven assertion.
Do not repeat a full review after a bounded repair unless it expands a trust, security, data or concurrency boundary.

merge.note: Judge safe serialized integration and proof on the integrated tree. Do not reward manual Git improvisation or extra cleanup.

required_outcomes.statement: Integrate exactly the frozen accepted source through the configured serialized merge route without bypassing the queue or lock.
Run the declared merge gate on the integrated tree, confirm the configured delivery target and retain or remove the source only according to policy.

known_risks.statement: A green source branch is not proof that the integrated target tree passes the merge gate.
Do not repeat a mutating merge command because a long-running operation is quiet; wait for progress or a terminal result.

e2e.note: Judge the complete chain for preservation, correction and code readiness. Stage quality and flow reliability remain separate vectors.

required_outcomes.statement: Preserve four-value/default, stable-order and narrow archived-project priority-only decisions through all stages without scope drift.
Complete CODE from the accepted work graph, close material CODE-REVIEW findings, integrate the frozen result through MERGE and prove the configured target tree.

known_risks.statement: Loss, invention or contradiction between durable handoffs is material even when individual stage artifacts look plausible.
